title: The AI Moment in Drug Discovery: Daphne Koller on The Long Run - TimmermanReport.com
gist: Podcast intro for The Long Run episode 213 with Insitro founder and CEO Daphne Koller, a first-generation AI drug discovery company that has raised $750 million from VCs and pharma partners including Bristol Myers Squibb, AstraZeneca and Gilead. The episode is framed as a reality check on what AI can and cannot yet do in drug discovery, with programs in fatty liver disease, ALS and brown-fat cardiometabolic markers.

insights.claim: Insitro, a South San Francisco AI drug discovery company founded in 2018, has secured $750 million in funding from venture capital firms and partnerships with big drugmakers.
insights.speaker: @ldtimmerman
insights.so_what: Shows the scale of capital first-generation AI drug discovery platforms have absorbed before clinical proof.

themes.theme: Data moat and the clinical trial hurdle

insights.claim: Insitro has spent years collecting and curating biological data to get to a point where AI is useful enough to approach human clinical trials, described as the most important hurdle in R&D.
insights.speaker: @ldtimmerman
insights.so_what: Implies AI drug discovery value depends on long-duration proprietary data building, and the real test is clinical translation, not model capability.

insights.claim: Daphne Koller offers a reality check on what AI can and cannot currently do for discovering new medicines, implying hype around AI drug discovery exceeds present capability.
insights.speaker: @ldtimmerman
insights.so_what: A leading founder tempering expectations suggests investors should discount near-term timelines for AI-derived drug approvals.
